card.name: Mid-clause words before a defining phrase
card.fires_on: Small connecting words, adverbs or punctuation partway through a long clause in philosophical or historical prose, where a defining or naming phrase may come next (like 'which is called').

modes.label: Adverbs and verbs mid-clause
modes.description: An adverb or verb inside an explanatory sentence about how something works or is defined.
modes.example: the image of the object on the retina is<< constantly>> in motion, slowly drifting and jumping back

modes.label: Commas, dashes and quotes
modes.description: Punctuation that interrupts a clause before the main statement continues.
modes.example: with reference both to individuals and peoples<< —>> arises only where the totemic level

modes.label: Linking words
modes.description: Words like which, as, or were that introduce a qualifying clause.
modes.example: it must have characters<< which>> shall enable us to distinguish it from other

card.writes: It promotes Chinese words meaning 'so-called' or 'called', suggesting a naming or defining phrase comes next.
card.plain: It fires in the middle of abstract, definition-style sentences, just before a term gets named or defined.
